Badrutt's Palace opens its winter season on 3 December 2026, 130 years after it first welcomed guests on the shore of Lake St. Moritz. The season runs until 30 March 2027.

## A family of pioneers

The Badrutt story starts with Johannes Badrutt, who founded the Kulm hotel in St. Moritz in 1855. His son Caspar Badrutt, born in Samedan in 1848, bought the Hotel Beau Rivage in 1864 and transformed it into Badrutt's Palace, officially opened in 1896. Caspar died in 1904, and his son Hans took over the management. Richard Leuenberger has been managing director since 2016.

The palace has long attracted fashion and society. Giorgio Armani was among its regular guests, and in 2025 GaultMillau named it Hotel of the Year 2026.

## A new chapter for winter 2026-27

This season brings a new bar inside Le Grand Hall by the Milanese designer Giuseppe Porcelli. Champalimaud Design is reworking rooms across several floors, creating larger rooms and suites and reducing the total number of keys. Martin Brudnizki Design Studio, which designed the original interiors, is refreshing La Coupole – Matsuhisa, set in the former tennis hall under a glass dome. These works follow the Serlas Wing by Antonio Citterio Patricia Viel, unveiled in winter 2024-25 with 25 rooms and suites.

The hotel holds three MICHELIN Keys and ranks No. 36 on The World's 50 Best Hotels 2026, the only ski and mountain resort on the main list.

## The signal

Grand alpine palaces do not stand still. At 130, Badrutt's Palace chooses to renew its rooms and bars rather than rest on its legend, and that is how a family name stays at the top of the Alps.

Happy 130th winter to the teams of Badrutt's Palace.
summary: Founded by Caspar Badrutt in 1896, the St. Moritz palace opens its 130th winter on 3 December with a new bar and reworked suites.
title: Badrutt's Palace at 130: the story behind St. Moritz's palace
why: An iconic alpine palace renews itself for its 130th winter.
